report.summary: Third round with the same critical: the configured boot (stored Wi-Fi) still aborts with "A stack overflow in task sys_evt" at the same boot point, even though CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE=4096 is now demonstrably in the build; the fresh-boot path and the display fix remain healthy.

deviceInfo.bootTime: fresh boot reaches the console ~2.1 s after reset; configured boot aborts ~1.7 s after reset
deviceInfo.chip: ESP32-S31 rev v0.0, 2 cores, 16 MB flash, 16 MB PSRAM
deviceInfo.connectivity: no broker peer on the emulator; onboarding SoftAP up when unconfigured; with stored Wi-Fi the panel still crashes right after MQTT init
deviceInfo.crash: stack overflow in task sys_evt (vApplicationStackOverflowHook, FreeRTOS port.c:730), emulator exit code 1
deviceInfo.freeHeap: not re-read on the crashed boot; ~12.5 MB free overall on the fresh boot

notes: Same signature, same boot point and the same instruction count as the two previous rounds (fault at I (1664), 'after 166699596 / 166697204 cycles'), so the newly added configuration produced no change in the emulated image's behaviour.

Evidence that the stack value is now genuinely compiled: sdkconfig.product contains ONLY CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE=4096, the build reports the resolved chain as sdkconfig.defaults + board_manager.defaults + sdkconfig.product, and the review verified 4096 in build/config/sdkconfig.h. Yet the overflow still happens, so the remaining suspect is that sys_evt does not own the overflow, or the emulated Wi-Fi stack calls into handlers with a much deeper native frame than 4 KB covers.

Other finding worth flagging: the committed sdkconfig.product's comment asserts that 'nothing of ours runs in-line on that task', but app_mqtt.cpp:244-248 still registers a dedicated wifi_connect_cb for STA_START via a second esp_event_handler_register (reported removed by the code-review evidence) — worth reconciling before the next attempt.
The display boot-loop fix stays solid across all boots: one setup pass, second init refused, panel + touch registered, no LVGL teardown, no assert.
artifacts/device.log covers this session: the fresh boot, the Wi-Fi/broker setup, and the configured reboot that crashed.
report.suggestedFix: The overflow is still on sys_evt at exactly the same boot point even though CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE=4096 is now in the built header, so the stack size alone (at 4 KB, and possibly the task attribution) is wrong. Instrument rather than guess: enable CONFIG_FREERTOS_USE_TRACE_FACILITY + CONFIG_FREERTOS_VTASKLIST_INCLUDE_COREID and CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_PANIC_PRINT_HALT (or a hardware stack guard image) and, on the first configured boot, capture the offending task's actual stack high-water mark before it dies (e.g. log uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark for sys_evt and mqtt_net after the Wi-Fi events, or raise CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE further, to 6144–8192, and re-test). The fix must be confirmed by two consecutive boots with stored Wi-Fi credentials both reaching 'Console ready' and 'ZeroCode AI firmware started' with no stack-overflow hook.

tests.details: mqtt-wifi + mqtt-broker save correctly, then a 'reboot' abortes with 'A stack overflow in task sys_evt has been detected' at the first Wi-Fi event after 'MQTT initialized'; the emulator exits (code 1) before app_logic/app_console, so a commissioned panel still dies on every power cycle. The build now contains CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE=4096 (verified via sdkconfig.product and build/config/sdkconfig.h) and no product handler is supposed to run in-line on sys_evt, but the crash is unchanged (same fault point, same cycle count).
tests.evidence: I (1634) W wifi: Password length matches WPA2 standards … / I (1664) app_mqtt: MQTT initialized (node 240ac4000001) / [WARN machine] Firmware abort on hart0: '***ERROR*** A stack overflow in task sys_evt has been detected.' / #1 vApplicationStackOverflowHook () at components/freertos/FreeRTOS-Kernel/portable/riscv/port.c:730 / [host] emulator stopped: esp-emu exited on its own (exit code 1)
tests.name: Boot with stored Wi-Fi credentials — no stack overflow / reset (previously failing)
